title: Efficient Inversion in Large Finite Fields GF(2m) Using Sliding-w FLT Framework
content: In the computation of multiplicative inversion over large finite fields GF(2m), the traditional approach commonly employs the Euclidean algorithm such that the number of operations is variable and difficult to predict, which may limit its computational efficiency in practical applications. This study proposes a new inversion method, called the sliding-w FLT method, for large finite fields based on a polynomial-basis representation to improve overall computational performance. The key behind this new method is that Fermat’s Little Theorem (FLT) and Horner’s rule are employed to segment the polynomial and expand the exponent, thereby reducing the number of finite-field multiplications. In addition, a lookup-table-based mechanism is incorporated into the exponentiation process to further reduce the computational overhead. Polynomial segmentation for the optimal value of w is determined. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared with conventional inversion methods, the proposed Algorithm 1 achieves performance improvements of up to 97.59% for GF(2571). Algorithm 2 developed on the restricted lookup tables shows up to 7.02× memory usage reduction over Algorithm 1 while the performance slightly reduces 1.69% for GF(2571) and w = 32. As a result, Algorithm 2 with the significant improvement of both computational benefits and memory efficiency makes it suitable for resource-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) platforms and dedicated hardware implementations.
